The father-in-law and mother-in-law of the 2nd respondent/complainant are before this Court,
calling in question the proceedings in C.C.No.8406 of 2022 pending before the XXIV Addl. CMM.,
Bangalore registered for offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504 and 506 r/w Section 34 of the IPC and Sections 3, 4 and 6 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

Heard Sri Adbhuth J Kaushik, learned counsel appearing for petitioner, Sri Thejesh P, learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for respondent No.1 and Sri Yathisha K J, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2.
3.

The marriage between the complainant and accused No.1 happens on 11-02-2015.

sentences.text: certain proceedings instituted between the two i.e., the husband and the wife.

Accused No.1/husband institutes proceedings invoking Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 seeking restitution of conjugal rights in M.O.P.No.63 of 2020 on the score that the wife has left the matrimonial house and want her back to the house.
Later, the complainant also institutes a petition for restitution of conjugal rights, in Bangalore, pending in M.C.No.2526 of 2020.

Therefore, there were two proceedings,
one by the husband, before the Court at Hosur NC: 2024:KHC:20422 and the other by the wife at Bangalore, both for restitution of conjugal rights.
4. It transpires, a joint memo was filed by the complainant and accused No.1/husband on 09-09-2021 and the complainant returns back to her matrimonial house.

After having returned,
comes the impugned complaint on 14-12- 2021 alleging torture and other harassment by the husband and in-laws.
The police after investigation, filed a charge sheet against all the accused in C.C.No.8406 of 2022.
Filing of the charge sheet has driven the petitioners to this Court in the subject petition.
5. The husband/accused No.1 is not before the Court.
Learned counsel for petitioners would submit that there are no allegations of any overt acts performed by the father-in-law or mother-in-law on the ground of demand of dowry.

Therefore, he would seek quashment of the proceedings against them, on the ground that there are omnibus statements which would not touch upon the ingredients of either Section 498A or Sections 504 and 506 of the IPC, as the case would be.

Per-contra, learned counsel for the 2nd respondent/complainant takes this Court through the summary of the charge sheet and the statement so rendered by the witnesses seeking to demonstrate that the torture was not only known to the members of the family, but even to the outsiders i.e., neighbours of the petitioners.
He would submit that it is a matter of trial for the petitioners to come out clean.

7. Learned High Court Government Pleader would also toe the lines of the counsel for the complainant in contending that the police have filed a charge sheet and the offences are met,
therefore, it is a matter of trial to come out clean.
8. I have given my anxious consideration to the submissions made by the respective learned counsel and have perused the material on record.
9. The husband and wife getting married is a matter of record and a child born from the wedlock on 10-12-2018, is NC: 2024:KHC:20422 also a matter of record.
The relationship turning sore resulting in two proceedings are again a matter of record.
The proceedings getting closed on 09-09-2021 on account of filing a joint memo.
It is from 09-09-2021 and 14-12-2021 is what forms the fulcrum of the complaint.

Though the narration of the complainant, in the complaint is what has happened right from 2015 to 2021, since the happenings are projected in the complaint and the complaint has lead to these proceedings, I deem it appropriate to notice the complaint filed by the 2nd respondent,
